recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

fields.Intro Paragraph 1: What if the reason you're stuck, sick, tired, or can't seem to break a pattern has less to do with your chemistry and more to do with your electrical charge? That's the thread Eileen McKusick has been pulling on for 25 years, and this conversation, recorded at her first-ever appearance on InnerVerse, is where it comes into full focus.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title":"Winning the Sovereignty Game","body":"Eileen frames this realm as a video game played on a prison planet, scattered with what she calls lobster pots, culturally set traps like debt, body issues, and low self-worth that are easy to fall into and hard to escape. Watching her sons circle the same level for lack of resources becomes her image for people stuck in inherited beliefs. Her stated mission is to free the humans, and she insists the work starts within: an activist who wants to heal the world's division has to face the inner critic and inner victim first, echoing the motto she keeps about emancipating ourselves from mental slavery."},{"title":"A Fractal Body Inside the Mind","body":"Chance introduces the superior brachium, a brain structure he learned about from Seven Bomar of Secret Energy that resembles a tiny body with arms outstretched, its head backing onto the pineal gland, and he offers it as the microcosm suggesting the body sits inside the mind. Eileen answers that everything is fractal: the biofield's toroidal shape repeats in a bar magnet, the Earth's magnetosphere, and the sun's heliosphere. She describes the field she works with as bounded by a plasma sheath of electric charge, a bubble of inaudible sound whose standing waves her tuning forks reveal like invisible ink decoders."},{"title":"Sound, Electricity, and the Sonic Slider","body":"Eileen admits she has never found a satisfying answer to what separates sound from electricity, and Chance offers lightning, where light, sound, and electric charge express a single event arriving through different senses. She explains the Circuit Boot's sixteen dimples as trapping vibration between skin and metal to deliver concentrated, coherent mechanical energy, and cites a study she attributes to Harvard in which mechanically stimulated tissue recovered two and a half times faster. She prefers the purely acoustic tool because, as a self-described sensitive, battery and plug-in devices feel to her like dirty electricity, while the fork simply adds tone that leaves the body toned."},{"title":"Distance Sessions and the Etheric Record","body":"Eileen recounts dismissing distance healing as a stupid question until an experiment on a physician friend in California, worked over an empty table, returned notes he called exactly right on. Losing the open line of communication forced her to trust subtler vibrational information, and she reports that group sessions and even recordings of them deliver the same reported benefits, with a distance study on anxiety involving ten volunteers now awaiting IRB approval. Her explanation runs through the ether, a timeless medium she equates with the Akashic record, from which she says she can pluck the file of a person and work on their hologram."},{"title":"The Voice as the Instrument","body":"In an experiment she says happened only the day before, Eileen set the forks aside entirely and toned with her voice until it began reflecting the dissonance in a friend's field, then became the stronger coherent signal that entrained the distortion clear. She frames it with the same resonance and entrainment mechanics she claims for the forks, and reports the recipient felt the voice working more powerfully than the forks themselves. Chance likens the forks to training wheels, which matches her own verdict: after twenty three years with tuning forks, she now holds that the power of one's own mind and voice is ultimately all anyone needs."}]
